column1: # Persian verb stems — infinitive <TAB> past stem(s) <TAB> present stem(s)
# Alternates are separated by "|". Where a verb's present stem triggers the
# glide rules after ب / ن / می (the standard, pp. 38-39), the surface alternate
# is listed second so the analyzer can match the written form without modelling
# the phonology: آمدن carries both آ and بیا-derived یا.
# Seed inventory. It is deliberately small and it is the bottleneck by design —
# evaluation L2 reports accuracy on known stems separately from coverage, so
# that "the rules are wrong" and "the lexicon is short" stay distinguishable.
# Sources: the standard grammars' paradigm tables; every entry is a form any
# Persian speaker can check, which is the one place in the rule base where
# citation is satisfied by universal agreement rather than a page number.
# Declined on purpose — do not "close" these gaps without reopening the ruling:
#   آر  as a present stem of آوردن.  Ruled out 21 September 2026. It is the
#   classical contraction of آور, and 90.6% of its 778 corpus occurrences are
#   Ganjoor verse; all 73 outside it were read and every one is the verb, so
#   adding it would be safe *for the می repair*. It is declined anyway, because
#   a stem is global: it would also make bare آرد analyze as a verb for every
#   other consumer, and آرد is the ordinary modern noun "flour" — the reading
#   we will meet more often as modern text enters the corpus. We are building
#   modern tools; آر is treated as the old variant it is. See Lab Note 016.
# (The file held 90, not the 113 quoted in Lab Notes 021 and 022 and in the
# programme register. 113 was this file's line count. Lab Note 015 had it
# right; Lab Note 023 carries the correction.)
# Nothing below was added from memory. Every entry has a source and corpus
# evidence, and the two are recorded separately because they fail separately.
#   mace   John Mace, *Persian Grammar: For Reference and Revision*, Appendix I,
#          'Irregular present stems of verbs', pp. 209-211, read from the scan
#          transliteration is what separates the two رفتن — raftan/rav- 'go'
#          from roftan/rub- 'sweep' — which the script does not.
#   class  Derived by a stated rule with a named exception list, not by eye:
#          ـیدن -> drop یدن · ـاندن -> drop دن · ـودن -> ـا · ـاختن ـیختن ـوختن
#          are listed with the rule. A class whose exceptions are unnamed is
#          not a rule, it is a habit.
# Every stem was then checked against corpus v5 (3.98M segments) for finite
# present forms *the verb's own past stem cannot also produce*. Without that
# subtraction می‌دید scores as evidence for a present stem دی, and بدید — the
# archaic ب-past — as four thousand more. A stem entered on three of the four
# cells م/د/یم/ند; `ی` was never counted, being the ezafe and the indefinite
# Rarity did not disqualify; ambiguity did. می‌پژوهد occurs once and is still
# proof, because nothing else spells that. Everything declined below is
# declined for ambiguity, never for being rare.
# DECLINED, with what the corpus actually said:
#   Preverb compounds — 115 of them: برداشتن، بازگشتن، برانگیختن، فروریختن.
#   The preverb separates under inflection and می lands inside it: بازمی‌گردد
#   occurs 211 times against می‌بازگردد twice. بازگرد is therefore not a string
#   the analyzer will ever meet, and adding it would paper over the real gap,
#   which is a missing morphological rule. This is now the largest single
#   Words that are not Persian verbs, each caught by reading its own evidence:
#     بایدن   Joe Biden. Seven hits, all modern Wikipedia prose.
#     درایدن  John Dryden, in the fa.wikipedia articles on Chaucer, Locke, Pope.
#     زدیدن   ز + دیدن. «دل نظارگیان آب شد ز دیدن تو» — Saeb, written solid.
#     گرودن   eleven hits, none verbal; its evidence بگراید is گراییدن's.
#   Verbs that are real but whose evidence is someone else's:
#     مزیدن   real in Rumi, but بمزد is mostly به + مزد, 'for wages'.
#     سربریدن سر incorporates and separates: سرمی‌برد 3, می‌سربرد 0.
#     باشیدن  a real verbal noun in Rumi, but its stem باش is بودن's — a second
# Two rulings that went the other way, both worth keeping:
#   فراختن  rejected here, overruled by Ali against Dehkhoda — correctly. The
#           rejection came from a SUBSTRING search that had counted افراختن's
#           own occurrences. It stands alone three times («سر فراختن», «قد
#           فراختن») and فرازد/بفرازد/فرازم inflect right through. Search by
#   اندودن  rejected on the same kind of false evidence (باندام is به + اندام),
#           then admitted on Dehkhoda («اندودن (مص) انداییدن») once انداید 14
# --- second pass: shapes with no class rule, each hypothesis read off the
# --- corpus one at a time. Admitted only on a ZWNJ می‌ form, which a noun does
# --- not produce: می‌بافند, می‌گشاید, می‌پندارند, نمی‌خسبد.
